```{r echo = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "##")
```

Imperial's [malariasimulation](https://github.com/mrc-ide/malariasimulation)
site files (built with the [site](https://github.com/mrc-ide/site) package, and
calibrated by foresite) describe each admin unit of a country: its calibrated
EIR, rainfall seasonality, mosquito species, and yearly treatment, bed net and
IRS coverage. `site_to_pipeline()` turns one unit into the arguments for
`pipeline()`, so `magenta` can start from the site's calibration rather than
fitting its own EIR.

The aim is to get `magenta` into the right transmission setting, and so in the
right ballpark, for scenario modelling of drug resistance. It is not a
reimplementation of malariasimulation's interventions: only treatment, bed nets
and IRS are used. SMC, PMC, vaccines and larval source management in the site
file are not modelled, and IRS uses `magenta`'s default efficacy whatever the
insecticide.

## Setting up a run

`site_to_pipeline()` takes one unit of a site file, from
`site::subset_site()`:

```{r setup, eval = FALSE}
library(magenta)
s <- readRDS("calibrated_scaled_site.rds")
k <- s$sites$name_1 == "Busia" & s$sites$urban_rural == "urban"
unit <- site::subset_site(s, s$sites[k, ])

dl <- drug_list_create(drugs = list(drug_create_al()))
args <- site_to_pipeline(unit, years = 2000:2024, burnin = 20, drug_list = dl)
out <- do.call(pipeline, c(args, list(N = 50000, seed = 1)))
```

The returned list holds:

* the site's EIR, and its seasonality (`site_seasonality()`), which is given to
  `pipeline()` directly through `seasonality`;
* a burn-in, 20 years by default, with no treatment, nets or IRS, so the run
  starts from the untreated equilibrium at the site's EIR (as the site's EIR is
  calibrated);
* the site's yearly bed net use, IRS coverage (times 0.75, as malariasimulation
  runs use) and treatment;
* bed net efficacy from `site::net_efficacy` at the unit's pyrethroid
  resistance, and species-weighted mosquito bionomics.

Its `year` attribute gives the calendar year of each simulated year. Drugs,
resistance, non-malarial fevers and barcodes are left to you: add them to the
list before calling `pipeline()`, and use the same `drug_list` that was given
to `site_to_pipeline()`.

### Treatment

The site's treatment coverage, `tx_cov`, is effective coverage, and
malariasimulation treats that fraction of clinical cases with a drug that
always works. `magenta` treats with real drugs, which can fail, so
`site_ft()` sets the proportion treated to
`ft = tx_cov / efficacy`, where efficacy is the drugs' baseline (no
resistance) chance of clearing the infection. Before there is resistance this
gives the site's effective coverage, and resistance then lowers it. The site
file's split of `tx_cov` into ACT and non-ACT drugs is not used, as both are
fully effective in malariasimulation.

### Bed nets

malariasimulation tracks each net from distribution, and its insecticide
decays as `exp(-t / gamman)`. The site's nets are topped up every year to
hold use at the site's values, and are kept for about the retention half-life
(825 days), so the nets in use at any time are a mix of ages. `magenta` has a
single bed net efficacy at each time, so `site_to_pipeline()` uses the
`"constant"` ITN decay clock (`itn_decay_clock` in
`model_param_list_create()`), which holds efficacy at its mean over a net life
of the retention half-life, with a half-life of `gamman * log(2)`.

## Comparison with malariasimulation

Two Kenya units were run in both models, from the Kenya site file in the
foresite calibration packet: Busia urban, the highest transmission unit in
Kenya (EIR `r round(24.35, 1)`), and Nyandarua rural, one of the lowest. Each
was run with 3 seeds, 50,000 people, a 20 year burn-in and then 2000 to 2024:

* `magenta` from `site_to_pipeline()`, treating with AL with no resistance and
  non-malarial fevers off;
* malariasimulation as foresite runs it, from `site::site_parameters()`.

The runs are too large for building the package, so were run on a cluster. The
scripts are in `vignettes_src/site/` in the package repository: `prepare.R`
cuts the two units out of the site file, `funs.R` has the two runs and their
yearly summaries, `setup.R` and `run.R` provision and submit the cluster tasks,
and `analyse.R` writes `vignettes_src/site_summary.rds`, which makes the
figures below.

```{r load}
library(ggplot2)

res <- readRDS("site_summary.rds")
runs <- res$runs
site <- res$site
unique(runs[c("model", "version")])

model_colours <- c(magenta = "#c51b7d", malariasimulation = "#2166ac")

# mean and range over seeds
summarise_runs <- function(var) {
  d <- stats::aggregate(runs[[var]], runs[c("model", "unit", "year")],
                        function(x) c(mean = mean(x), lo = min(x), hi = max(x)))
  cbind(d[c("model", "unit", "year")], as.data.frame(d$x))
}

plot_runs <- function(var, ylab, site_var = NULL) {
  d <- summarise_runs(var)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(year, mean, colour = model, fill = model)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
    geom_line() +
    facet_wrap(~unit, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_colours) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = model_colours) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab, colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  if (!is.null(site_var)) {
    p <- p + geom_point(aes(year, .data[[site_var]]), data = site,
                        inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 0.8)
  }
  p
}
```

### Interventions

```{r interventions, fig.height = 4}
iv <- rbind(
  data.frame(site[c("unit", "year")], input = "Treatment (tx_cov)", value = site$tx_cov),
  data.frame(site[c("unit", "year")], input = "Bed net use", value = site$itn_use),
  data.frame(site[c("unit", "year")], input = "IRS coverage", value = site$irs_cov)
)
ggplot(iv, aes(year, value, colour = input)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~unit) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Coverage", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Prevalence

The points are the site file's PfPR2-10 (the Malaria Atlas Project estimates
the EIR was calibrated to). Lines are the mean over seeds and the band is their
range.

```{r prevalence}
plot_runs("pfpr_2_10", "PfPR2-10 (microscopy)", "site_pfpr")
```

### Clinical incidence

```{r incidence}
plot_runs("clinical", "Clinical cases per person per year")
```

```{r incidence-05}
plot_runs("clinical_05", "Clinical cases per child under 5 per year")
```

### Differences

```{r differences}
d <- summarise_runs("pfpr_2_10")
w <- reshape(d[c("model", "unit", "year", "mean")], idvar = c("unit", "year"),
             timevar = "model", direction = "wide")
w$diff <- w$mean.magenta - w$mean.malariasimulation
stats::aggregate(cbind(mean_abs_diff = abs(diff), mean_diff = diff) ~ unit,
                 data = w, FUN = mean)
```

Over 2000 to 2024 `magenta` follows malariasimulation's trends in both units:
prevalence falls as treatment and bed net use rise, and both models show the
rise in 2018 when Busia's net use dropped. The two are closest at low
transmission: in Nyandarua rural prevalence differs by about one percentage
point. In Busia urban the models are close at the start (PfPR2-10 0.52 against
0.49 in 2000), but `magenta` falls more slowly as interventions scale up, so by
2024 it is about 5 percentage points higher (0.24 against 0.19).

Clinical incidence differs more. At similar prevalence, `magenta` has about 20%
more clinical cases in 2000. In the later years, after mass net campaigns, the
gap grows: in Busia urban in 2024 `magenta` has 0.42 cases per person per year
against malariasimulation's 0.17, and 0.78 against 0.33 in children under 5.
Some of this is likely from the bed nets. malariasimulation gives everyone
fresh nets at each mass campaign, and their efficacy then decays. `magenta`
holds efficacy at its mean over a net life, so it misses the drop in
transmission after each campaign. The rest has not been worked out, and is
worth looking at before using clinical incidence from `magenta` runs set up
this way.

Both models are well below the site file's PfPR2-10 in Busia urban in 2000 to
2004 (about 0.5 against 0.54 to 0.98), and from 2005 on both are close to it.
malariasimulation is below it too, so this
comes from how the site was calibrated, or from how these runs differ from
foresite's (for example the burn-in), rather than from `magenta`.

Overall, `site_to_pipeline()` puts `magenta` in the right transmission setting.
Prevalence is in the ballpark of malariasimulation, which is what is needed as
the starting point for scenario modelling of drug resistance. Clinical
incidence after net campaigns should be treated with care.

A `magenta` run took about 70 minutes and a malariasimulation run about 35
minutes (50,000 people, 45 years).

## Rerunning the comparison

From a copy of `vignettes_src/site/` on the cluster share:

1. set the `magenta` commit in `pkgdepends.txt` and run `setup.R`,
2. run `prepare.R` (locally, with the share mounted) to cut the units out of the
   site file,
3. submit the runs with `run.R` (12 tasks, each about an hour),
4. run `analyse.R` to write `site_summary.rds`, copy it to `vignettes_src/`,
   and rebuild this vignette with
   `Rscript vignettes_src/build_vignettes.R SiteFiles`.
